title: Segment API pipeline with read/write sharding to reduce contention and tail latency
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Refactor the console backend API aggregation pipeline by splitting read (query/aggregation/reconciliation) and write (streaming events, state updates) pathways and introducing a lightweight sharder to reduce lock contention and GC spikes. This reduces p99/p95 tail latency for dashboard endpoints and decreases CPU contention on aggregation workers. Additionally upgrade GraphQL server dependency to 17.x and clean up cache adapters to support a two-tier hot/cold prefix cache.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Kickoff: scoped after perf spike observed during customer demo (2026-02-28). Initial hypothesis: aggregation worker locks and large monolithic request bus cause GC churn and tail latency.
2026-03-02 - Engineering spike: bench harness created (bench/console-agg) to replay production traces at 1x/5x load. Baseline p95=420ms, p99=1.2s for /api/console/summary under 5x.

2026-03-04 - Design decision: split pipeline into three logical stages: ingress (validation + auth), read-aggregation (query + materialized joins + summarization), and write-stream (ingest events, update caches). Introduced an in-memory sharder keyed by customer_id with lock-free queues per shard.

2026-03-05 - Trade-offs discussed in #infra-perf: sharder reduces contention but increases memory footprint (~150MB per 1000 active shards). Decided acceptable for Dedicated customers; added feature flag to gate rollout.

2026-03-06 - PR open: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/2048 — implements sharder, split handlers, upgrades graphql-js to 17.0.2. Notes: server API surface unchanged; internal handler registration refactored.

2026-03-07 - Code review by Elena Kirov: requested clearer metrics emission for per-shard queue length and backpressure path; asked to add integration test for KV cache TTL eviction under high write load.

2026-03-08 - Bench after change: p95=260ms (-38%), p99=600ms (-50%) on bench replay at 5x; CPU steal reduced by 22%. Memory increase observed as expected. See bench results: https://benchboard.redwood.ai/runs/console-agg-seg-20260308

2026-03-09 - Rollout plan approved: canary 2% traffic for 24h then 25% if no errors, followed by 100% over 48h. Feature flag key: segmented_api_pipeline_v1. Monitoring dashboards: console/perf/segmented_pipeline_canary.
Follow-ups: ENG-80422 (instrumentation of hot-tier cache eviction metrics), ENG-80423 (auto-scale policy per-shard worker), ENG-80424 (cleanup old monolithic pipeline and remove legacy adapters).
